enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
608 AM MDT Fri Oct 16 2026

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...


.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 548 AM MDT Fri Oct 16 2026

 - A strong backdoor cold front is moving through tonight, 
   bringing gusty winds and well below normal temperatures into 
   the weekend. 

 - High Wind Warning is in effect for far west Texas and portions
   of southern New Mexico into Friday. Wind gusts to 60 mph are 
   possible along mountain west slopes. 

 - Scattered rain showers for the middle of next week as 
   temperatures rebound. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 949 PM MDT Thu Oct 15 2026

A potent cold front is pushing through the Borderland this evening, 
bringing strong NE winds behind it. Gusts over 50 mph have 
already been seen E of the US 54 corridor. The strength of the 
sfc high behind the front is more in-line with what we tend to see
in the middle of winter (1045mb-ish over central high plains on 
Fri). This will result in an impressive pressure gradient across 
the CWA as the front sweeps through in the near-term. West mtn 
slopes will see the gustiest winds, reaching 60 mph or higher. The
strongest winds are expected to occur from now through early Fri 
AM with winds easing a bit during the day on Fri and shifting 
more easterly. Generally 25-35 mph sustained winds are modeled 
with a pocket of lighter winds from Las Cruces up towards Holloman
AFB. No changes have been made to the wind headlines. Forecast 
remains on track.

Dust models, including the RRFS and NOAA AQ model, show a signal for 
blowing dust through the overnight, favoring S Otero County and far 
west TX. Low chance of 1 mile VIS in isolated areas, most likely in 
El Paso County. Any dust lifted off White Sands should get blocked 
by the San Andres and struggle to reach the upper RGV. The dust 
threat lowers Fri AM and shifts out W towards the Lordsburg Playa
where winds remain strong. Confidence is lower in seeing dust 
impacts in Hidalgo Co compared to eastern areas, where BLDU 
Advisories are in effect until 9am Fri.

An upper low cuts off from the flow off the Baja coast for the rest 
of the week, pulling moisture into it. A ridge of high pressure 
extends from the NW at the same time, keeping most of the moisture 
to our south. Precip chances remain near zero into the weekend as 
winds subside through Sat. The upper low opens up into a shortwave 
on Sun, bringing some of its moisture into the region and slight 
rain chances for western areas. Then, a Pacific storm system dives 
down the West Coast, pulling more subtropical moisture northward 
through midweek from the Pacific. PWs climb towards 1" with low-
medium rain chances area-wide late in the period. A low flood 
threat is present as NBM 90th %-ile shows 24-hr rain amounts of 
1-2" Wed and Thu. Confidence is low in impacts for this midweek 
rain event.

Temperatures crash to unseasonably cool levels (highs 10-20 degrees 
below normal) behind tonight's front. Lowland highs in the low-mid 
60s are forecast through Sat with cold air advection ongoing. It'll 
feel more like winter than early fall, especially in the Sacs Fri AM 
as wind chills reach the teens. Lowland areas to the N and E are
likely to dip into the 30s Sat AM with patchy frost. Temperatures
rebound towards normal early next week.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 548 AM MDT Fri Oct 16 2026

The strong winds will continue for most of the day, but things
will finally slowdown later this evening. We will see occasional
lower visibilities due to blowing dust. But visibilities are
expected to stay at VFR conditions. KELP has some high clouds, but
those will move off later this morning and we will have unlimited
ceilings this afternoon into the overnight hours. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 548 AM MDT Fri Oct 16 2026

A cold front ushered in strong winds and some blowing dust this
morning. These elevated winds will continue through most of the 
day, before slowing this evening. Min RH's today and Saturday will
be in the mid to upper teens in the lowlands and in the 20's in 
area mountains. Sunday will start both a warming trend and 
moisture will return to the region. Rain chances will be back in 
the forecast for much of next week, with min RH's above 30% across
the area. Ventilation rates today will be very good to excellent 
and then a little lower on Saturday.

&&
